walkthroughs.body_html:
Waves & Particle Nature of Light — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Waves & Particle Nature of Light brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Waves & Particle Nature of Light.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Diffraction through a gap is most noticeable when the gap width is:
options: About the same size as the wavelength
Much larger than the wavelength
Exactly half the amplitude
Gap size makes no difference

mcqs.q: Which observation supports the particle (photon) model of light?
options: Diffraction through a slit
Interference fringes
Polarisation of light
The threshold frequency in the photoelectric effect
Electrons are photons.
Waves carry no energy.
Electrons have no mass.
Particles can behave as waves.

mcqs.q: Increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency:
options: Raises the metal's work function.
Still releases no photoelectrons.
Releases electrons after a short delay.
Releases electrons with higher energy.

mcqs.q: Can very bright light below the threshold frequency release photoelectrons?
options: No — each photon still lacks the energy to overcome the work function, however many arrive.
Yes — sufficient intensity will eventually free electrons.
Only protons diffract, not electrons.
Yes — after about a minute of warming up.

mcqs.q: Is light a wave or a particle?
options: Yes — after about a minute of warming up.
It must be one or the other, and experiments will eventually settle which.
It shows both behaviours — interference reveals its wave nature; the photoelectric effect reveals its particle nature.
It is neither — light is a kind of very fast sound.
Yes — electron beams produce diffraction rings, showing matter has a de Broglie wavelength.
No — diffraction is only for waves like light, not for particles.
Only protons diffract, not electrons.
It is neither — light is a kind of very fast sound.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Amplitude”?
options: The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle, greatest when the gap is about one wavelength wide.
Electron emission from a metal requires light above a threshold frequency — key evidence for the photon model.
Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
The maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its equilibrium position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photoelectric effect”?
options: Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
Light energy arrives in discrete packets — photons — each of energy E = hf.
Electron emission from a metal requires light above a threshold frequency — key evidence for the photon model.
The number of complete oscillations per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Wave-particle duality”?
options: Light energy arrives in discrete packets — photons — each of energy E = hf.
The number of complete oscillations per second, measured in hertz (Hz).
Electron emission from a metal requires light above a threshold frequency — key evidence for the photon model.
Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Diffraction”?
options: Electron emission from a metal requires light above a threshold frequency — key evidence for the photon model.
The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle, greatest when the gap is about one wavelength wide.
Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
The number of complete oscillations per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Frequency”?
options: The number of complete oscillations per second, measured in hertz (Hz).
Light energy arrives in discrete packets — photons — each of energy E = hf.
Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
The maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its equilibrium position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photon model”?
options: Electron emission from a metal requires light above a threshold frequency — key evidence for the photon model.
Light energy arrives in discrete packets — photons — each of energy E = hf.
Light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour; electrons diffract, with de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle, greatest when the gap is about one wavelength wide.

mcqs.q: A wave completes 20 oscillations in 4 seconds. What is its frequency?
options: 5 Hz
80 Hz
24 Hz
0.2 Hz
